checks.Title: Re-enter through change, not summary
checks.Evidence: The opening leans heavily on explicit backstory recap rather than a changed present carrying the memory: 'She'd built it the year after Wennick, after one wrong call came back as a look she still couldn't shake' and later 'At the diner near the Spine, the morning after Axiom, it had been five who carried the truth...Six wasn't cleaner. Six had a stranger in it' — these are direct summary-mode exposition dumps explaining what happened rather than letting the present state (the rule, the crew, the count) imply it.
checks.Fix: Cut the explicit Wennick/Axiom explanations and let Rook's present behavior (the three-steps hesitation, the counting ritual, her wariness of Adalemo) carry the history without narrating the backstory that produced it.

checks.Title: Reintroduce names like an old friend would
checks.Evidence: Some returning-cast introductions land exactly right (Boiler introduced 'reading a crack in a load-bearing column the way another man reads a letter he's carried too long,' Scout 'in four places up there, and not one of them was the roof her body sat on') — these are efficient, in-voice tags. But others front-load dossier-style backstory instead: Lace's entrance leans on abstract analysis ('She came in the way she came into everywhere — sideways to the doorframe... present where the cost was lowest') before any concrete defining action, and Vox is introduced mid-scene via technical function ('two fingers resting on the seam... feeling the four channels') without a single grounding gesture a lapsed reader could hook 'right, her' onto until much later.
checks.Fix: Give Lace and Vox one immediate, physical, defining beat on first appearance (the way Boiler gets the column and Scout gets the rooftop) before pivoting into the analytical description of how they operate.

checks.Title: Refresh proprietary terms on a lighter touch than the gateway
checks.Evidence: Proprietary terms like 'PEREGRINE,' 'the Lake Platform,' 'Wennick,' 'the Loop,' and 'Class V pathway' are dropped in with only glancing context (e.g., 'whether PEREGRINE had gone quiet or only quiet-sounding') that assumes the reader already carries the referent, while other terms like 'Greymark Unseen jacket' or 'ArcSec' get a quick functional gloss ('filed no proximity contact with their readers') that does the re-teaching work well.
checks.Fix: Give the recurring proper nouns most load-bearing to backstory (Wennick, the Lake Platform, PEREGRINE's prior incarnation) at least one clause each that re-teaches their meaning through context, the way the Greymark jacket line already does, rather than trusting bare recall.

checks.Title: Never an acronym before its term
checks.Evidence: Acronyms like 'NSB'-style terms appear bare with no prior full-term gloss: 'GLMZ' is used repeatedly (e.g., 'At that hour the GLMZ was all lit surface') with no expansion ever given, and 'ArcSec' appears ('A pair of ArcSec sat on a cart') with no full term preceding it, as does 'PEREGRINE' functioning like an org/program acronym-style proper noun introduced bare ('whether PEREGRINE had gone quiet').
checks.Fix: Insert the full expansion in-voice at first use, e.g. introduce 'the Greater Lakes Metro Zone — the GLMZ' and 'Arcturus Security, ArcSec for short' before the bare acronyms are used again.

checks.Title: Pay the previous book its due, then move
checks.Evidence: The opening pages are dense with unglossed callbacks to prior events (Wennick, the Lake Platform, Axiom's Class V division, the diner near the Spine, the five-vs-six count comparison, PEREGRINE, Stave) that are treated as load-bearing emotional history without ever pausing to confirm to a first-time or returning reader what was won or lost and why it should land as weight; the text relitigates the rule/Wennick material repeatedly (the rusted-door metaphor recurs at least three times) rather than banking it once and moving forward.
checks.Fix: Replace the recurring abstract callbacks to Wennick/the rule with one concrete, early, self-contained beat that shows what the previous book's ending cost or won Rook, confirms it stuck, and then let the narrative move on without re-explaining it later.

checks.Title: Open the door the last ending left ajar
checks.Evidence: The prose leans heavily on prior events (Wennick, Lake Platform, Axiom, the 2206 tile, Rook's rule) as texture, but the 'ajar door' from the previous book is never named as a single clear question early on — instead the reader is dropped into a dense web of backstory (Adalemo's rail fall, the formula, the five-vs-six count) that reads as continuity-for-returning-readers without a legible single thread being reopened and complicated for someone tracking 'what happens in this city' from book one.
checks.Fix: Add an early, explicit line naming the specific unresolved question the last book ended on (e.g., what Rook actually decided about Adalemo, or what became of the formula) before burying it under new complications, so returning readers immediately recognize the reopened thread and newcomers get a clean hook.

checks.Title: Reward the long memory without taxing the short one
checks.Evidence: The prose leans heavily on unglossed prior-story events treated as load-bearing context — 'the year after Wennick,' 'the last job' where the rule slipped, 'the Lake Platform,' 'the diner near the Spine, the morning after Axiom' with 'five who carried the truth about the formula,' and Rook's fraught unresolved history with Adalemo ('a man she'd put in the lake once, in a storm, off a failed rail') — none of which are explained enough for a first-time reader to grasp their emotional stakes, yet the current plot's tension (why the rule matters, why six vs. five is a big deal, why Adalemo's loyalty is such a live question) depends on feeling their weight.
checks.Fix: Add brief in-scene grounding for each callback the moment it's invoked — e.g., a sentence clarifying what happened with Wennick, what the Axiom formula secret actually was, and what passed between Rook and Adalemo at the rail — so newcomers get the necessary emotional context without needing the previous book, while returning readers still get the deeper resonance.

checks.Title: Escalate, don't repeat
checks.Evidence: The heist escalates past the original engagement's stakes into new moral terrain: Vox discovers the wall she's cracking isn't PEREGRINE's target but Ohara's own buried atrocity-cover-up (sixty-one names, forty reconciled, twenty-one erased), forcing a real-time ethical choice (reseal vs. expose) that has no precedent in 'the last job,' and the story adds a genuinely new intimacy problem (Ohara's memory gap, the 'did it open?' repeated twice) and a new structural wrinkle (a sixth person, an enemy operative, now holding crew secrets) that a repeat of the Axiom job could never produce.
